nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a discrete probability distribution on $\alpha \times \beta$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are measurable spaces. The mutual information of the probability measure defined by $p$ is $0$ if and only if this measure equals the product of the probability measures defined by the two marginals of $p$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $m$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of the $\sigma$-algebra of $\Omega$, and let $c \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The quantized conditional entropy given $m$ of the constant observation $\omega \mapsto c$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Constant quantized observations have zero conditional entropy

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and let $m$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of the $\sigma$-algebra of $\Omega$. The quantized conditional entropy given $m$ of the observation that is constantly $0$, with values in the one-element set $\{0\}$, is $0$.
nodes.title: One-valued observations have zero conditional entropy

nodes.title: Conditional entropy of a finite observation given a sub-$\sigma$-algebra

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are finite, and let $p_X$ be its first marginal. Write $H(X, Y)$ for the Shannon entropy of $p$, $H(X)$ for the Shannon entropy of $p_X$, and $H(Y \mid X) = -\sum_{a, b} p(a, b) \log_2 (p(a, b) / p_X(a))$ for the finite conditional entropy of $p$, all in bits. Then $H(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y \mid X)$.
nodes.title: Chain rule for entropy

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are finite, with marginals $p_X$ and $p_Y$. Writing $H$ for Shannon entropy in bits, $H(p) \le H(p_X) + H(p_Y)$.
nodes.title: Subadditivity of entropy

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
